lines.trans: Did a heavy truck just drive down Calle de los Tilos, Mateo?
No trucks drive by at midnight. Look through the lobby glass: lightning!
Oh no! You took all four shutters off their hinges after sanding them!
And right now they are leaning unpainted against the courtyard wall!
If the dry wood gets wet tonight, Monday's green paint will not stick!
Grab the back door lantern, Clara: the first big drops are already falling!
I have the left end of the first one: lift and run toward the hallway!
Good! Two inside and two left outside: watch the wet stones!
We got the last pair in just as the sky opened up! Whew, my sleeves are soaked!

words.gloss: we got inside; we brought in

lines.trans: The wood is completely dry, Clara. You move fast in a storm.
Wait: if it rains hard all Monday, where do we paint four tall shutters?!
Look at Monday's forecast... heavy rain until Tuesday at noon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

agarrar.gloss: to grip; to stick; to take hold

meanings.en: to grip; to stick; to take hold
meanings.note: Said of paint or glue adhering to dry wood, as well as gripping with the hand.

examples.text: La pintura nueva agarra muy bien sobre madera seca.
examples.trans: Fresh paint sticks very well on dry wood.

examples.text: Agarra fuerte el otro extremo de la mesa.
examples.trans: Grip the other end of the table firmly.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Mi hermano es muy alto.
examples.trans: My brother is very tall.

examples.text: Las ventanas de esta casa son altas.
examples.trans: The windows in this house are tall.

apoyar.gloss: to lean; to rest; to support

meanings.en: to lean; to rest; to support
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; apoyar algo contra la pared means 'to lean something against the wall'.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera con cuidado contra el ladrillo.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder carefully against the brick.

examples.text: Apoyamos las sillas dobladas debajo del arco.
examples.trans: We lean the folded chairs under the arch.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Metal hinge on a door or lid.

examples.text: La bisagra está aquí.
examples.trans: The hinge is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bisagras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hinges from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: With se + indirect object (se le cayó), expresses accidental dropping.

examples.text: La lluvia cae sobre el tejado.
examples.trans: The rain falls on the tiled roof.

examples.text: Se me cayeron las monedas.
examples.trans: I accidentally dropped the coins.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: Vivo en una calle muy tranquila.
examples.trans: I live on a very quiet street.

examples.text: Cruza la calle con cuidado.
examples.trans: Cross the street carefully.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent in the plural: camiones.

examples.text: Un camión grande descarga cajas frente al mercado.
examples.trans: A big truck unloads boxes in front of the market.

examples.text: Por esta calle estrecha casi no pasan camiones.
examples.trans: Hardly any trucks drive down this narrow street.

meanings.note: ¡Santo cielo! means 'Good heavens!'.

examples.text: El cielo está aquí.
examples.trans: The sky is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cielos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the skys from the door.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Formed from femenina completa + -mente.

examples.text: La calle está completamente tranquila.
examples.trans: The street is completely quiet.

examples.text: Lo había olvidado completamente.
examples.trans: I had completely forgotten it.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Indicates physical contact or contrast.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera contra la pared.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder against the wall.

examples.text: Los farolillos brillan contra el cielo.
examples.trans: The lanterns glow against the sky.

meanings.note: Wooden outer or inner shutter hinged beside a window.

examples.text: Cierra las contraventanas por la noche.
examples.trans: Close the shutters at night.

examples.text: Las contraventanas de madera son verdes.
examples.trans: The wooden shutters are green.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Refers to window glass or crystal.

examples.text: Cuidado, el vaso es de cristal.
examples.trans: Careful, the glass is made of crystal.

examples.text: Limpio los cristales de las ventanas.
examples.trans: I'm cleaning the window panes.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.text: Avísame cuando llegue el taxi.
examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: ¡Cuidado con el perro!
examples.trans: Watch out for the dog!

examples.text: Lleva la tarta con cuidado.
examples.trans: Carry the cake carefully.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.text: Hay cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: There are four tables inside.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.text: Hablamos después del desayuno.
examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.

examples.text: ¿Qué hacemos después de eso?
examples.trans: What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: From empapar ('to soak through').

examples.text: Llegamos del patio con los abrigos empapados.
examples.trans: We came in from the courtyard with soaked coats.

examples.text: Cambia ese trapo empapado por uno seco, por favor.
examples.trans: Swap that soaked cloth for a dry one, please.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Doorway or entrance hall.

examples.text: Te espero en la entrada del museo.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you at the museum entrance.

examples.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada?
examples.trans: How much is the ticket?

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Plural faroles; classic wrought-iron courtyard lantern.

examples.text: Encendemos los faroles del patio al caer la tarde.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at dusk.

examples.text: El farol de hierro alumbra toda la escalera.
examples.trans: The iron lantern lights up the whole staircase.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Mi padre es muy fuerte.
examples.trans: My father is very strong.

examples.text: Hoy hace un viento fuerte.
examples.trans: There is a strong wind today.

meanings.note: Ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: Cae una gota de lluvia en mi mano.
examples.trans: A drop of rain falls on my hand.

examples.text: Solo quiero unas gotas de leche.
examples.trans: I only want a few drops of milk.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: a la izquierda = on the left; la mano izquierda = the left hand.

examples.text: Me duele el pie izquierdo.
examples.trans: My left foot hurts.

examples.text: Escribe con la mano izquierda.
examples.trans: She writes with her left hand.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.text: Siéntate a mi lado.
examples.trans: Sit next to me.

examples.text: La farmacia está al lado del banco.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is next to the bank.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

meanings.note: To smooth wood with sandpaper (la lija).

examples.text: Hoy vamos a lijar la mesa vieja.
examples.trans: Today we are going to sand the old table.

examples.text: Primero lijo la puerta y luego la pinto.
examples.trans: First I sand the door and then I paint it.

meanings.note: Impersonal stem-changing verb (o -> ue: llueve).

examples.text: Hoy llueve mucho en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is raining heavily in Valencia.

examples.text: Anoche llovió hasta las diez.
examples.trans: Last night it rained until ten.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lluvia.
examples.trans: We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el lunes, los lunes.

examples.text: El lunes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Monday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lunes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mondays from the door.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La mesa es de madera.
examples.trans: The table is made of wood.

examples.text: Me gusta el olor de la madera.
examples.trans: I like the smell of wood.

meanings.note: Subirse las mangas means 'to roll up one's sleeves'.

examples.text: Súbete las mangas de la camisa antes de fregar.
examples.trans: Roll up your shirt sleeves before scrubbing.

examples.text: La lluvia repentina me mojó las dos mangas.
examples.trans: The sudden rain got both my sleeves wet.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el martes, los martes.

examples.text: El martes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Tuesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los martes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Tuesdays from the door.

meanings.note: A medianoche means 'at midnight'.

examples.text: La tormenta de verano empezó justo a medianoche.
examples.trans: The summer storm started right at midnight.

examples.text: A medianoche todo el barrio queda en completo silencio.
examples.trans: At midnight the whole neighbourhood falls completely quiet.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Opposite of seco (dry).

examples.text: Es una pieza mojada.
examples.trans: It is a wet piece.

examples.text: Porque las contraventanas de madera mojadas suavizan el eco de los adoquines...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: La lluvia moja los adoquines grises.
examples.trans: The rain wets the grey cobblestones.

examples.text: Perdón por mojar la entrada con el paraguas.
examples.trans: Sorry for wetting the entrance with my umbrella.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.text: El muro está aquí.
examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.text: ¡Oh, ahí está la puerta azul!
examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Plural los pares (dos pares de gafas = two pairs of glasses).

examples.text: El par está aquí.
examples.trans: The pair is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pairs from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: The corridor inside a house, hotel or train.

examples.text: El baño está al final del pasillo.
examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.

examples.text: No corras por el pasillo.
examples.trans: Don't run in the corridor.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el patio.
examples.trans: The children play in the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos en el patio cuando hace sol.
examples.trans: We have breakfast in the courtyard when it's sunny.

meanings.note: Describes a heavy suitcase, wrench, or coat.

examples.text: Es una pieza pesada.
examples.trans: It is a heavy piece.

examples.text: Cerrada y vaciada. Pásame la llave inglesa pesada de tu izquierda.
examples.trans: Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La casa tiene paredes de piedra.
examples.trans: The house has stone walls.

examples.text: Hay una piedra en mi zapato.
examples.trans: There's a stone in my shoe.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: En primavera pintamos la puerta azul.
examples.trans: In spring we paint the blue door.

examples.text: El abuelo pintó una llave dorada.
examples.trans: Grandfather painted a golden key.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: Necesitamos pintura blanca para el baño.
examples.trans: We need white paint for the bathroom.

examples.text: Me encanta la pintura española.
examples.trans: I love Spanish painting.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: Cierra la puerta, por favor.
examples.trans: Close the door, please.

examples.text: Alguien llama a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone is knocking at the door.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.text: Solo quedan dos habitaciones libres.
examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

quitar.gloss: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)

meanings.en: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)
meanings.note: Quítate el abrigo = take off your coat; quitar el polvo = dust.

examples.text: Quito el polvo del tablero de madera.
examples.trans: I wipe the dust off the wooden board.

examples.text: Quítate el abrigo mojado y pasa.
examples.trans: Take off your wet coat and come in.

meanings.note: Flash of light in the sky, followed by el trueno ('thunder').

examples.text: Un relámpago iluminó de repente todo el patio.
examples.trans: A flash of lightning suddenly lit up the whole courtyard.

examples.text: Vimos dos relámpagos lejanos detrás de las colinas.
examples.trans: We saw two distant flashes of lightning behind the hills.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.text: El tren es muy rápido.
examples.trans: The train is very fast.

examples.text: Hablas muy rápido, más despacio, por favor.
examples.trans: You speak very fast; more slowly, please.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.text: La ropa ya está seca.
examples.trans: The clothes are already dry.

examples.text: Prefiero el vino seco.
examples.trans: I prefer dry wine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.text: El tiempo está aquí.
examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Heavy rainstorm with wind, thunder, and lightning.

examples.text: Guardamos los cojines antes de que empiece la tormenta.
examples.trans: We put the cushions away before the storm starts.

examples.text: Después de la tormenta el patio huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: After the storm the courtyard smells of wet earth.

meanings.note: Opposite of delantero ('front'); la puerta trasera is 'the back door'.

examples.text: Entramos con las cajas por la puerta trasera.
examples.trans: We came in with the boxes through the back door.

examples.text: Las ventanas traseras dan a una calle muy tranquila.
examples.trans: The back windows look onto a very quiet street.

meanings.note: Natural exclamation of effort, relief, or sudden heat/rain.

examples.text: ¡Uf, cuánto pesa esta contraventana de madera maciza!
examples.trans: Whew, how heavy this solid wood shutter is!

examples.text: ¡Uf, entramos en el pasillo justo antes del chaparrón!
examples.trans: Phew, we got into the hallway right before the downpour!

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Me gusta el té verde.
examples.trans: I like green tea.

examples.text: Las contraventanas son verdes.
examples.trans: The shutters are green.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.

examples.text: Soy yo, abre por favor.
examples.trans: It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.text: Es el último tren de la noche.
examples.trans: It's the last train of the night.

examples.text: Vivo en el último piso.
examples.trans: I live on the top floor.
